tasks.short: Oversee gameplay testing against the original vision

steps.what: Record gameplay testing issues on the form
Read the original vision before testing
Draft the adherence sheet from vision fields

loop.output: adherence sheet that cites only those ids
loop.check: Every cited vision-point id is on the vision list
loop.stop: One pass, then leave a blank where an issue has no vision-point id
loop.why_not_simpler: Issue prose does not map to a vision point by a fixed rule

steps.what: Oversee the gameplay session in the room
Sign the intended experience finding
File the signed experience finding

tasks.design: Testers log issue id, build id and vision-point id on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts an adherence sheet that may cite only those ids. The game designer still oversees the gameplay session, then signs one finding version before it is filed on the {PROJECT} board.
tasks.previous_blocker: Session notes were free text, so a later reader could not tell which vision point a complaint was about.
tasks.enabler_now: A vision point can be an id on the form, so the sheet can check that every cited point exists.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the session felt like the intended experience is still a call made in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides if the session matched the vision, including when the issue log is clean but the play felt wrong.

ambition.what: Record an adherence finding after every gameplay session, not only at the milestone review

tasks.altitude: Playtests stay on the calendar. The week loses recopied notes. The designer can refuse a finding that cites a vision point nobody logged.

reach.task: Retest the build against the signed finding
reach.learn: Which vision points failed this session and which were not played

evidence.claim: In a mid-size studio this task is mostly sitting with a playtest and then writing what failed. The hard part is the feel of the session, not the formatting of the note.
A checklist can list vision-point ids from a form. It cannot decide that a session matched the intended experience. That call stays with the designer who was in the room.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when a signed session finding is filed. Running the next build is a later task.

Input contract: session id, build id, vision-point id, issue id, tester id, and pass or fail as the tester stated it. Producer is the quality assurance analyst. If a vision-point id is missing, the sheet leaves a blank and the designer does not sign that row. The same fields can be typed from a paper note and marked manual.
Use the document store template and the work board form before custom code. The playtest is not replaced. This design does not record tester performance.
unknowns: Who signs when the designer misses the session.
Which board is the record of findings.
research_questions: What share of session notes cite no vision point?
How often does a clean issue log still get a fail on feel?

already_counted.description: Designer rewrites adherence rows that cite a weak or missing vision point
Designer time in the playtest stays inside the session and is not deducted again

incremental.description: Keep vision-point ids aligned when the vision document is restructured
Testers correct issue rows the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: session finding version signed after this playtest
the same signed session finding version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most sessions still arrive as unmarked notes, so the designer writes the finding by hand. The high case assumes the form is used but every session is still watched and signed. Tester hours are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Present design concepts to management and colleagues

steps.what: Draft design concepts from the form fields

loop.input: concept fields and the pack template
loop.output: outline whose mechanic and risk match the form
loop.check: Each mechanic name equals the submitted field
loop.stop: Stop a section that has no mechanic name
loop.why_not_simpler: How to argue the concept in the room is not a field

steps.what: Artists and animators comment on the pack
Invite technical colleagues and programmers
Present design concepts to management
Sign which concepts the room accepted
File the concepts version that was accepted

tasks.design: The designer enters concept name, audience, mechanic and open risk on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded outline in {DOCS} drafts the concept pack from those fields only. The presentation to management, artists, animators and programmers stays in the room, and only the accepted concept version is filed on the {PROJECT} board.
tasks.previous_blocker: Concept packs were rebuilt from old slides, so the room could accept a line that was no longer the design.
tasks.enabler_now: Concept name, mechanic and risk can be fields, so the outline can be checked against the form.
tasks.still_hard: Winning the room, and knowing which objection is fatal, stays a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The designer chooses which concept to defend and which objection to accept.

ambition.what: Record the accepted concept version at each presentation, not only in the milestone deck

tasks.altitude: The presentation stays. Less time is spent rebuilding the pack. The designer can refuse to file a concept the room did not accept.

reach.task: Build only the concept version the room accepted
reach.learn: Which concept was accepted and which risks are still open

evidence.claim: Presenting a concept in a mid-size studio is a room with artists, animators, programmers and management. The pack is preparation. The hard part is the conversation.
An outline can repeat mechanic and risk from a form. It cannot tell which objection the room will treat as fatal.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when the accepted concept version is filed. Building the concept is out of scope.

Input contract: concept id, audience, mechanic name, open risk, decision accepted or not, and decider role. Producer is the game designer. If the mechanic name is empty the outline stops. A verbal decision is typed after the meeting and marked manual.
Use the document template before custom code. The presentation is not recorded or scored. Colleague time in the room is not the designer workload.
unknowns: Who may accept a concept if the studio manager is absent.
Whether the artists in the room are staff or freelancers.
research_questions: How often does the filed concept differ from what was said in the room?
How many packs have no mechanic name?

already_counted.description: Designer edits the pack where the form fields are too thin
Presentation time stays in the room and is not deducted again

incremental.description: Update the concept pack template when a new risk field is required
Artists resend a comment that was not tied to a concept id

approvals.approved_version: concept version accepted in this presentation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes packs are still written as prose, so the outline does not fire and the designer still builds the pack. The high case assumes the form is used but every presentation and acceptance stays in the room. Colleague time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare concept layouts and three-dimensional mock-ups

steps.what: Read the concept brief for this layout
Prepare two-dimensional concept layouts
Build the three-dimensional mock-up
Review the layouts with the designer
Sign which layouts to keep
File the layouts that were signed

tasks.design: The brief stores layout id, view name, scale note and what must be readable, on a {DOCS} template. The game designer still prepares the layouts and the three-dimensional mock-up in {OTHER}, the graphical design software. A colleague review stays in the room, and only the signed layout version is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Layouts lived as loose files with no brief id, so a later build could use a picture that answered a different question.
tasks.enabler_now: A layout id and a brief id can travel with the file, so the review is about one version.
tasks.still_hard: The drawing itself, and whether the mock-up reads at a glance, stays with the designer.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides the composition and which version is clear enough to build from.

ambition.what: Mark one layout version as the one artists may build from, each time a mock-up changes

tasks.altitude: Drawing time barely moves. The gain is a signed layout version instead of a file name. The designer can refuse a picture that has no brief id.

reach.task: Build the scene from the signed layout
reach.learn: Which layout version is current and which views are still open

evidence.claim: Concept layouts and mock-ups in a mid-size studio are drawn by the designer in graphical software and then shown to a colleague. The picture is the work.
A file can carry a brief id and a version label. That does not draw the layout or the mock-up, and this task does not ask a model to draw it.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when the signed layout version is filed. Scene art is a later task.

Input contract: layout id, brief id, view name, scale note, dimension as two or three, and status. Producer is the game designer. A picture with no brief id is not filed. If the brief is only verbal, the designer types the view name and marks it manual.

The meeting prior treats time at the screen with a colleague as a meeting. The statement is the drawing. The review is the meeting. The graphical tool export and the document store version label are tried before custom code. No step generates the picture.
unknowns: Which graphical tool is the studio standard.
Whether a technical artist owns the three-dimensional file instead of the designer.
research_questions: What share of layout files have no brief id?
How often does a review send the layout back?

already_counted.description: Drawing time on the layouts stays in the remaining work and is not deducted again
Mock-up time stays with the designer and is not deducted again

incremental.description: Keep the brief fields aligned when a new view type is added

approvals.approved_version: layout version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes briefs stay verbal, so version labels are typed by hand and drawing time is unchanged. The high case assumes ids exist but every layout and mock-up is still drawn and reviewed by a person. Artist build time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep up with design techniques and audience needs

steps.what: Review current literature on design techniques
Log audience interests and reactions
Spend time talking with colleagues about industry trends
Spend time attending educational programs and conferences
Draft which audience needs to carry forward

loop.output: note that cites source ids only
loop.check: Every cited source id is on the reading list
loop.stop: One pass, then drop any line with no source id
loop.why_not_simpler: Which need matters is not a lookup on the title

steps.what: Sign the techniques note for the month
File the signed techniques note

tasks.design: The designer saves a source id, medium and topic into a {DOCS} reading list that a {BI} view can filter. A bounded note drafts a monthly techniques note only from items marked worth a look. Conferences, workshops and talks with colleagues stay in person, and the designer signs which technique to try.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clippings lived in mail and chat, so a monthly note could not show which source a claim came from.
tasks.enabler_now: A saved item can carry a source id, so a note can be checked against the list.
tasks.still_hard: Judging which audience reaction matters, and what a conference actually implied, stays with the designer.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides which technique is worth a trial on the current game.

ambition.what: Choose one design technique to try each month, not only after a conference

tasks.altitude: Less time hunting old links. Conferences and colleague talks stay. The designer can drop a note line that has no source id.

reach.task: Spike the technique the designer marked for a trial
reach.learn: Which technique was chosen and which sources were rejected

evidence.claim: Keeping up with game design is reading, talking with colleagues, and going to workshops and conferences. Only the reading list is a record the studio can file.
A note can be limited to source ids the designer already saved. It cannot decide which audience need matters for the current game.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when a signed techniques note is filed. Trying the technique in a prototype is a later task.

Input contract: source id, title, medium as literature or colleague or workshop or conference, topic, and a worth-a-look flag. Producer is the game designer. Items with no source id are not cited. A conference takeaway is typed afterwards and marked manual.
The document list and a filtered view are configured before custom code. No feed is treated as a complete picture of audience needs. Attendance is not logged as staff performance.
unknowns: Which sources the studio already pays for.
Whether conference notes may be stored in the document store.
research_questions: What share of notes cite no source?
How often is a chosen technique actually tried?

already_counted.description: Reading time on the literature list stays inside remaining time
Conference time stays with the designer and is not deducted again

incremental.description: Retire source ids that no longer resolve and fix the note template

approvals.approved_version: techniques note signed for this month

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes sources stay as loose links, so the note is still written by hand. The high case assumes the list is used but every conference, workshop and colleague talk still happens, and the designer still picks the technique. Travel and attendance are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Playtests, concept presentations and layout reviews stay in the week. Reading lists and session sheets stop being recopied. The designer signs the finding, the accepted concept and the layout version.
reach: Quality assurance analysts receive the signed session finding instead of a verbal recap.
Software developers receive the accepted concept version and the technique marked for a trial.
skills_to_grow: State a vision point as an id a session sheet can check.
Separate a concept the room accepted from a pack that was only shown.
Keep a layout file tied to the brief it answers.
role.ambitious_version: Every playtest ends with a signed finding, every concept review names an accepted version, and each month one technique is chosen from a sourced list.
